text_blocks.snippet: Decompression sickness (DCS), also known as "the bends," is a condition caused by dissolved gases forming bubbles in the body's tissues and bloodstream due to a rapid decrease in ambient pressure. This most commonly occurs in divers ascending too quickly, but can also affect high-altitude aviators or individuals working in pressurized environments. The bubbles can obstruct blood flow, trigger inflammation, and damage tissues, leading to a range of symptoms.
snippet_highlighted_words: a condition caused by dissolved gases forming bubbles in the body's tissues and bloodstream due to a rapid decrease in ambient pressure

list.title: How it happens:
list.snippet: When a person is exposed to increased pressure, like during a deep dive, gases (primarily nitrogen) dissolve into their body tissues and fluids. If the pressure decreases too rapidly (e.g., during a quick ascent), these dissolved gases can come out of solution and form bubbles.
